focus: A22 plugin bridge drift: dualPlugin coverage of .opencode/plugins entry files, hard-coded plugin lists in the v2 test suites and doctor battery, bridge event/hook mapping coverage, README and mirror sync

label: No v1-only plugin remains on main: every one of the 16 regular .opencode/plugins/*.js entry files builds its default export through dualPlugin (grep -L flags only the sk-vision.js symlink, a designed exception), but no test, script or doctor check enumerates the directory and fails on a non-dual entry, so the invariant that kept session-relaunch v1-only from recurring is enforced nowhere

Both v2 suites pin hand-maintained plugin lists instead of enumerating the directory: PLUGIN_NAMES (12 names) in tests/v2-registration.test.cjs:19 and the PLUGINS array (5 names) in tests/v2-hard-plugins.test.cjs:28; the union happens to cover all 17 entry files today, but a new entry file lands in neither list by default and passes CI with zero v2 coverage — the same failure shape that let session-relaunch.js reach main with only an OpenCode 1 factory

sk-vision.js is a symlink to a dist bundle with a native v2 setup and a chat.message hook key outside MAPPED_HOOKS, documented in plugins/README.md:181 as not going through the bridge; a guard implemented as the focus's naive grep -L dualPlugin check would fail this designed exception, so the guard policy must classify entries (bridge consumers vs exceptions manifest) rather than test one literal

cleanup.skippedKeys is the bridge's only signal for silently dropped hook keys outside MAPPED_HOOKS (recorded at v2-bridge.js:280, never logged or failed), and the suites assert it exactly once, for the designed chat.message exception in v2-bridge.test.cjs:632; no test asserts skippedKeys is empty for any of the 16 bridged plugins, so a plugin adding an unmapped hook key would be inert under OpenCode 2 yet fully green in CI

Plugins gate core behavior on event names whose live OpenCode 2.0.32 delivery is explicitly unverified (README.md:65): the bridge maps only session.text.ended->message.part.updated and session.step.ended->message.updated (plus two aliases) and forwards every other type verbatim from the stream, but session.created (session-cleanup trigger at session-cleanup.js:247, opencode-goal.js:3222, system-deep-loop-guard.js:67, codex-hooks-watchdog.js:78) and disposal names (server.instance.disposed, global.disposed) are exercised only against stub streams; session-relaunch's message.updated/message.part.updated/session.idle gates are covered by the two mappings and the alias, answering the focus question affirmatively for that plugin

plugins/README.md:77 claims the v2-registration suite covers 11 plugins while the suite's PLUGIN_NAMES holds 12 and the read-only run this iteration reports tests 12 — a concrete instance of hand-maintained-count drift; the .cursor/commands/doctor-*.md battery contains no plugin mention at all, so the focus's expected doctor count pin could not be located; .hermes/SYNC.md governs mirror drift per-surface (generated copies under --check, one hand-authored plugin mirror validated behaviorally), so mirrors were never designed to track the OpenCode plugin file list

The synthesized message.part.updated in the bridge is a lossy reconstruction: fixed role assistant, text parts only (v2-bridge.js:22); no currently bridged plugin consumes other part types, so this is a latent restriction for future consumers, not an active defect

direction: Guard design that fails on any .opencode/plugins entry file lacking the literal dualPlugin export, with no exception mechanism
reason: sk-vision.js is a symlinked dist bundle with a native dual export by design (README.md:181), covered separately by the hard suite; a literal-only guard fails the designed exception and would force a wrong remediation

direction: Treating README/mirror desync of the plugin file list as an integration bug
reason: .claude and .codex consume plugin logic through hooks on shared .cjs cores, not plugin copies, and .hermes/SYNC.md explicitly scopes its one plugin mirror to behavioral parity with its own validate manifest; the only real sync defect found is the README's own suite count (README:77 vs 12 tests)
